## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Input** | Live coral fragments (on tiles) |
| **Output** | One glutaraldehyde-fixed, decalcified polyp per fragment for TEM, plus a homogenate of the remaining polyps for symbiont density |
| **Time** | Fixation ≥ 24 h (up to 6 months) → decalcification hours to days → polyp dissection |
| **Tested on** | *Galaxea fascicularis* |
| **Imaging** | Processed and imaged by the University of Miami Miami Project to Cure Paralysis TEM Core |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Safety
Z-fix (10% aqueous buffered zinc formalin) is **toxic**. Work in a fume hood with full PPE (goggles, lab coat, gloves, closed shoes). The stock container is heavy, so move it with two people. Read the Z-fix [product information](http://www.anatechltdusa.com/files/130912398.pdf) and [SDS](http://www.anatechltdusa.com/files/114169364.pdf) first. When diluting acid, always add **acid to water**.
:::

## Materials

- Z-fix concentrate (Anatech); glutaraldehyde (provided by the TEM core, store at 4 °C)
- Concentrated HCl; DI water
- 0.2 µm filtered seawater (FSW): vacuum filter unit + pump
- 15 mL and 50 mL tubes, specimen containers, glass bottles, funnel
- Labeled plastic jugs/bins for formalin and acid waste
- Ruler or scale bar, camera; scalpel, Petri dish; parafilm

## Solutions to prepare

| Solution | Recipe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **0.2 µm FSW** | Vacuum-filter seawater into a glass bottle | ~1 L per filter run |
| **Diluted Z-fix** | 1 part Z-fix : 4 parts FSW | Mix in a labeled jug in the fume hood. TODO: the original labels say "25% zinc formalin", which would be 1:3. Confirm the ratio. |
| **10% HCl** | 900 mL DI water, then add 100 mL HCl | Acid into water, never the reverse |

## Procedure

### A. Plan and label

1. Randomly choose the fragments to fix (e.g. one per tank) and record their tile IDs.
2. Label tubes or containers with tile ID, tank, treatment, species, initials, date **and** the chemical ("Z-fix in FSW").
3. Volumes: **30–40 mL** fixative per 50 mL tube, or **350–450 mL** per specimen container. Pre-fill before sampling.

### B. Fix

4. Photograph each fragment in seawater with a scale bar.
5. Remove the coral from the tile and lower it gently into the fixative without splashing. Top up until it is fully covered.
6. Store cool and dark (flammables fridge) for **at least 24 h**. Samples can stay in Z-fix for **up to 6 months**.

### C. Decalcify

7. Pour the Z-fix into the formalin waste container.
8. Refill with the **same volume of 10% HCl**. Leave the cap **off** (CO₂ is released).
9. Replace the HCl every **24 h** until the skeleton is completely dissolved (hours to days, depending on size).

### D. Dissect and post-fix

10. Pour off the HCl, put the tissue in a plastic Petri dish, and photograph it with a scale bar. Note which polyp you take.
11. With a scalpel, cut out **one polyp** and put it in a 15 mL tube with **2 mL glutaraldehyde**, fully submerged. Cap, parafilm and store at **4 °C** until delivery to the TEM core.
12. Count the remaining polyps, put them in a 15 mL tube with **5 mL FSW**, homogenize, and store at 4 °C for [symbiont density](symbiont-density-hemocytometer.qmd).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Fragment not fully covered | Container too small or fragment too large | Add fixative until covered, or use a specimen container |
| Decalcification very slow | HCl spent | Replace the acid every 24 h; larger fragments take days |
| Tissue too fragile to dissect | Over-long acid exposure | Check daily and stop as soon as the skeleton is gone |
